chunks: And by this chain, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Sinān, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān, who said:

I heard Abā Baṣīr saying: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: From where did the companions of ʿAlī come to attain what came upon them, despite their knowledge of their deaths and their tribulations?

He said: So he answered me, as if angered: From whom would that be except from themselves? So I said: What prevents you, may I be made your ransom? He said: That is a door that was closed, except that al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, may the blessings of Allah be upon them both, opened a small part of it.
Then he said: O Abā Muḥammad, those people had stoppers upon their mouths.

key_terms.أَوْكِيَةٌ: fastenings or stoppers, indicating restraint and withholding speech
key_terms.بَابٌ أُغْلِقَ: a matter or access that was closed off
key_terms.شِبْهَ الْمُغْضَبِ: in a manner resembling one who is angered
key_terms.مَنَايَاهُمْ: their appointed deaths or times of death

ai.seo_question: How did the companions of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام know about their deaths and tribulations?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the special knowledge possessed by the companions of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding their deaths and tribulations. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام indicates that such knowledge came from themselves in a restricted manner, and that this was a closed door, with only a slight opening associated with al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليهما السلام. It also emphasizes that those companions were marked by restraint and secrecy.
